Get the credential Connect Verify Node reference Troubleshooting On this page Overview Prerequisites Create a Gumroad application and access token Connect to Mattering Verify it works Node reference Using the integration Troubleshooting The Mattering Automations Gumroad integration puts Gumroad's v2 API on your automation canvas: list and create products and their variants, read sales and refund them, manage license keys, run discount codes and custom checkout questions, draft, preview, schedule and send audience emails, add steps to workflows, keep the media library, and read payouts, annual earnings and tax forms. Eighty one nodes in total, thirty three that read and forty eight that act, covering every operation Gumroad documents. The credential is a single access token that you generate in your Gumroad account settings. There is no plan to buy first: Gumroad sells no subscription plans at all, charging a per-transaction cut with no monthly fee, so no tier gates API access and any account can create an application and issue itself a token. The decision that carries weight is not the token, it is the scopes on the application behind it, because Gumroad's own reference says the account scope covers most endpoints while narrower ones refuse an account only token. Three things about this API shape every workflow built on it, and all three are easier to read now than to hit later. Responses from the v2 API are enveloped with a success flag, and a rejected request can answer HTTP 200 with that flag set to false. Pagination is an opaque cursor with no page number and no page size parameter anywhere. And every money column on a sale is in the minor units of that row's own currency, which makes totalling across a mixed currency window wrong in two different ways at once. All three are explained in full below, and this guide ends with the complete node reference. Before you start A Gumroad account. Any account will do. Gumroad has no subscription plans, so there is no tier requirement here and nothing to upgrade. Its published pricing is per transaction and nothing monthly: 10 percent plus 50 cents on sales through your own profile and direct links, and 30 percent when a new customer finds you through the Discover marketplace. API access is not billed at all. An application created in the applications area of your Gumroad account settings, and an access token generated from it for your own account. The token is a single opaque string with no expiry and no refresh cycle. A decision about which Gumroad account holds the connection. Every node runs as that seller, so a refund is issued from their balance, an audience email arrives from their name, and a rotated license key breaks whatever their customer already installed. The right scopes on that application. Gumroad lists ten: account, view_profile, edit_profile, edit_products, edit_emails, view_sales, view_payouts, view_tax_data, mark_sales_as_shipped and edit_sales. Gumroad states that account gives full access to most endpoints, and that endpoints with a narrower security boundary, media being its own cited example, refuse an account only token and require the specific scope named on the endpoint. Every node in this integration names the scope its endpoint documents. A separate account to build against, if you intend to exercise the write nodes. The write paths here touch real commerce: a refund moves money to a real person, a published email reaches a real audience, and a rotated license key breaks a customer's installed software. A throwaway Gumroad account with a self-purchase is the honest test environment, since Gumroad documents no sandbox. For the tax form and annual earnings nodes, a United States seller with the tax centre enabled. Those endpoints are documented as United States only, so a token that works everywhere else can still find nothing here. A Mattering workspace with access to the Automations app. Create a Gumroad application and access token Gumroad issues API credentials from your own account settings rather than from a separate developer portal, and there is no review queue, no partner programme and no billing gate in front of it. What you create is an application, and what you paste into Mattering is an access token generated from that application for your own account. The part worth slowing down on is the scopes, because Gumroad fixes what a token can reach at the application, and a scope miss surfaces as a refusal on a credential that otherwise works perfectly. Sign in to Gumroad and open Settings , then Advanced , where the application form lives. Create a new application. Give it a name you will recognise in six months, since this is the record you will come back to when a node is refused. Set the application's scopes to cover the nodes you intend to use. For broad read and write coverage that means account together with the specific scopes the narrower endpoints require. Do not assume the account scope is enough. Gumroad's own reference states that account gives full access to most endpoints, and that endpoints with a narrower security boundary refuse an account only token and require the specific scope noted on the endpoint. Media is the example Gumroad itself cites: the three media library nodes need view_profile or edit_profile specifically. A missing scope is the most likely reason a correctly built workflow fails. Generate an access token for your own account from the application and copy it. This is the single string Mattering needs. The token has no expiry and no refresh cycle, so there is nothing to renew on a schedule. It is a bearer credential in the plain sense: anyone holding it can act as the seller, including refunding sales and sending audience email, so treat it accordingly. Connect Gumroad to Mattering In Mattering Automations, open Connectors and click Add Connector . Choose Gumroad from the list. Click Create new credential , paste the access token, and save it. The token is stored encrypted in Google Secret Manager. The connector registers it with the run's redaction context the moment it reads it, and scrubs both the raw token and its percent-encoded form out of anything that can reach node output or a log line, because the token is also sent as a request parameter and an HTTP library exception can quote a URL. Click Test Connection . Mattering calls Gumroad's user endpoint, which takes no parameters and is the cheapest authenticated call on the API. It sends the token both ways, as an Authorization bearer header and as an access_token request parameter, exactly as every node does, so a pass proves the path the nodes actually take rather than one half of it. A pass proves the token, not your scopes. Gumroad's account scope does not reach every endpoint, and the tax form and annual earnings endpoints additionally need a United States seller with the tax centre enabled. If a specific node is refused on a credential that just passed this test, the scope named in that node's description is the first thing to check. All 81 Gumroad nodes appear in your canvas palette. Verify it works Open any automation canvas and check the palette: a Gumroad section should list the read and action nodes. Drop Gumroad: Get User onto the canvas and run a test step. It is the natural probe because it takes no parameters and answers the question that matters before any write: which seller this connection acts as. Two fields on the response are conditional rather than missing, and knowing that saves a false alarm: the email address appears only for a token holding view_sales, and the profile URL appears only once a username is set. Now run Gumroad: List Products without changing anything. This is where most Gumroad workflows start and it is the source behind every product picker in the integration, so a populated result is a second confirmation that the credential and the pickers are both fine. Two shape notes while you are here. The url field is documented by Gumroad as deprecated and always null, so read short_url instead. And the sales count and sales total fields appear only when the token holds view_sales or account, so their absence is a scope fact rather than a product with no sales. Open the product picker on a node such as Gumroad: List Variant Categories and confirm it populates with product names and prices rather than raw ids. The dependent pickers are worth a look too: choosing a product narrows the variant category picker, and choosing both narrows the variant picker. Everything in this verify path is read-only, so it cannot reach a refund, an audience send or any of the ten deletes, and it is safe to re-run whenever you want to check the connection. Node reference 81 nodes, generated from the connector itself so this reference always matches what ships. Read and query nodes 33 Gumroad: Download Tax Form gumroad_download_tax_form Download the PDF of one tax form. This is the ONLY endpoint on the Gumroad API that does not return JSON on success: it answers with the raw PDF bytes and a Content-Disposition attachment header, and only switches to a JSON error envelope when it fails. This node therefore returns the file's metadata and its bytes base64 encoded rather than a parsed object, so it can be written to storage or attached to an email by a following node. Anything larger than 8 MB comes back as metadata only, because a very large base64 blob would bloat every downstream node input. The document contains the seller's tax identity, so treat the output as sensitive. US only, tax centre enabled, and requires the view_tax_data scope. Gumroad: Get Annual Earnings gumroad_get_earnings Fetch the annual earnings breakdown that matches the totals in Gumroad's own Tax Center: gross, fees, taxes, affiliate credit and net, all in the smallest currency unit, for one tax year. FULLY REFUNDED SALES ARE EXCLUDED from every aggregate, so this will not equal a naive sum of the sales list, and that is correct rather than a discrepancy. US only, tax centre enabled. A year outside the seller's available range, which runs from the account creation year to last year, returns 404. Requires the view_tax_data scope. Gumroad: Get Email gumroad_get_email Fetch one audience email in full: subject, HTML body, audience type, state, publish and schedule times, and its recipient and audience counts. Requires edit_emails or account. Gumroad: Get Offer Code gumroad_get_offer_code Fetch one discount code by id, with its coupon text, its discount and how many times it has been redeemed. As with the lister, a fixed amount code carries amount_cents and a percentage code carries percent_off. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Get Payout gumroad_get_payout Fetch one payout, optionally with the sale ids it covers and with a full transaction ledger matching the exported payout CSV. The transaction list is the useful part for reconciliation: each entry carries a type, date, purchase id, item and buyer, taxes, shipping, sale price, Gumroad fees and net total, and the types include Sale, Chargeback, Full Refund, Partial Refund, the PayPal and Stripe Connect refund and affiliate variants, and the payout transfers themselves. Note that transactions are OFF by default while sales are ON. Requires the view_payouts scope. Gumroad: Get Product gumroad_get_product Fetch one product in full. This returns everything the lister returns plus custom_html, the custom landing page, so it is the read half of the custom landing page workflow. It is also the only place to see a product's covers and attached files. Note that each attached file comes back as a TIME LIMITED SIGNED download URL rather than the canonical file URL, and the canonical URL cannot be recovered from a read, so a workflow that attaches files must keep the URL that Gumroad: Complete File Upload gave it. Requires view_profile, edit_products or account. Gumroad: Get Profile Custom HTML gumroad_get_profile_custom_html Read the seller's custom profile landing page: the stored source HTML, the rendered HTML, whether a landing page is in effect and the public profile URL. Gumroad keeps only the latest version with no history, so this node plus your own version control is the whole backup story for that page. Gumroad: Get Public Product Page gumroad_get_public_product_page Read the public display data for ANY Gumroad product page, with no credential at all. This is the read counterpart to the authenticated product nodes: it returns exactly what the rendered page shows, meaning price, covers, description, variants, ratings and the refund policy, and it never exposes buyer, seller private or analytics fields. Because it needs no token it works against products you do not own, which makes it the node for competitor and catalogue monitoring. Note the response has NO success key: it is a bare object with an api_version, so branch on the HTTP status rather than on success. Gumroad: Get Public Profile gumroad_get_public_profile Read any creator's public profile with no credential: display name, bio, avatar, social links and the products shown in their public profile sections. Seller private fields such as email, balance and tax information are never included. Like the public product page, the response has NO success key, so branch on the HTTP status. Gumroad: Get Refund Policy gumroad_get_refund_policy Read the account level refund policy: the period, the display title derived from it, the fine print and whether it is IN EFFECT. Read in_effect before writing anything, because it decides which of two mutually exclusive systems is live: when it is true the account policy governs and per product refund_period values are refused, and when it is false the product level fields govern and updating this policy is refused. Gumroad: Get Sale gumroad_get_sale Fetch one sale in full. The detail shape is RICHER than the lister's and the extra fields are the ones a finance workflow actually needs: tip_cents, the tax label and whether tax was included, the payment processor and its transaction id and fee, the buyer's review, and a buyer_presentment block giving what the customer was actually charged in their own currency with the FX rate used. Requires view_sales. Gumroad: Get Subscriber gumroad_get_subscriber Fetch one subscriber by id, with their product, email, purchase ids, recurrence, license key and the cancellation, end and failure timestamps that decide whether the subscription is still alive. Note the response key is the plural subscribers even though it holds a single object, which is a Gumroad quirk rather than a typo here. Requires view_sales. Gumroad: Get User gumroad_get_user Fetch the authenticated seller's own account: name, bio, user id, profile picture and profile URL. Two conditional fields worth knowing about because their absence is not an error: email only appears for a token holding view_sales, and url only appears once a username is set. This is also the cheapest way to confirm a credential works, which is what the connector's auth test uses. Gumroad: Get Variant gumroad_get_variant Fetch one variant by id: its name, its price difference in the smallest currency unit and its purchase cap. Requires view_profile, edit_products or account. Gumroad: Get Variant Category gumroad_get_variant_category Fetch one variant category by id. The category record itself is just an id and a title; to see the options inside it use Gumroad: List Variants. Requires view_profile, edit_products or account. Gumroad: Get Workflow gumroad_get_workflow Fetch one active workflow with every email step in it and each step's delivery statistics: sent count, opens, open rate, clicks and click rate. This is the only place the step ids appear, so run it before editing a step. Requires edit_emails or account. Gumroad: List Categories gumroad_list_categories Fetch Gumroad's full product category tree, flat, with each entry's id, name, human label, full path and parent id. This is the lookup behind the category field on product create and update: Gumroad wants the PATH, for example design/ui-and-web/figma, not the label. It is also the source for the category picker on both product write nodes, so run it once and the pickers fill themselves. Gumroad: List Custom Fields gumroad_list_custom_fields List the extra questions a product asks a buyer at checkout, each with its name and whether it is required. The name is the identifier as well as the label, so this is the node to run before updating or deleting one. Note the shape quirk: required comes back as the STRING false rather than a boolean. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: List Emails gumroad_list_emails List the seller's audience emails with their state, audience type, schedule and recipient counts. Filter with type to see only published, scheduled or draft. This is the source for every email picker in this connector, and the node to run first when auditing what is queued to go out. Requires edit_emails or account. Gumroad: List Media Files gumroad_list_media List the images in the account's media library, newest first, with each file's id, name, extension, size, hosted URL and status. The library exists because custom product and profile pages render under a Content Security Policy that BLOCKS images loaded from other sites: only inline data images and Gumroad's own asset hosts are allowed, so an image hosted anywhere else simply will not appear. Upload it here first and embed the URL this returns. Files belong to the account rather than to one product, so the same image can be reused everywhere. Requires view_profile specifically: this is the endpoint family Gumroad names when it says an account only token is refused. Gumroad: List Offer Codes gumroad_list_offer_codes List a product's discount codes with how many times each has been used. The response shape varies per row and that is the thing to wire around: a fixed amount code carries amount_cents and a percentage code carries percent_off, never both, so read whichever is present rather than assuming one. A universal code is one that applies to every product on the account, and those appear here too. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: List Payouts gumroad_list_payouts List the seller's payouts with amount, currency, status, creation and processing timestamps, the processor used and a masked bank account or PayPal address. Statuses seen here include payable, pending, completed and failed. One row can be unlike the others: the upcoming payout is included by default and carries a NULL id, because it has not happened yet, so any workflow keying on id has to handle that or turn include_upcoming off. Requires the view_payouts scope. Gumroad: List Product Reviews gumroad_list_product_reviews List the reviews shown on one of your product pages, newest first, with the rating, the buyer's message, the purchase id and your own published response if you left one. Only PUBLICLY VISIBLE reviews are returned, meaning a buyer left a written message or an approved video: a star only rating with no message still counts towards the product's average_rating but never appears here, so the row count and the review count on the product page will not agree. Up to 100 per page. Available with any read scope. Gumroad: List Product Subscribers gumroad_list_product_subscribers List the ACTIVE subscribers to one membership or subscription product, with each one's email, purchase ids, recurrence, license key and lifecycle timestamps. Reading the state is the part that catches people out: a subscription is TERMINATED if any of failed_at, ended_at or cancelled_at is set and in the past, so those three have to be checked together rather than trusting one. The status field is one of alive, payment_method_update_required, pending_cancellation, pending_failure, failed_payment, fixed_subscription_period_ended or cancelled. Pagination is opt in here, unlike the rest of this API: without paginated the endpoint returns everything, and with it the page is capped at 100. Requires view_sales. Gumroad: List Products gumroad_list_products List every product on the authenticated seller's account, with price, currency, publication state, tags, category, thumbnail and the whole variant tree for tiered memberships. This is the node most Gumroad workflows start from, and it is the source for every product picker in this connector. Two shape notes worth knowing before wiring to it: url is documented as deprecated and always null, so read short_url instead, and sales_count and sales_usd_cents only appear when the token holds view_sales or account. The list shape also differs from the single-product shape, which adds custom_html. Requires view_profile, edit_products or account. Gumroad: List Resource Subscriptions gumroad_list_resource_subscriptions List the account's active webhook subscriptions FOR ONE RESOURCE. The resource name is required, so there is no way to see every subscription in a single call: to audit them all, run this once per resource across the eight supported names. Each row carries the subscription id needed to remove it. Gumroad: List Sales gumroad_list_sales List the seller's successful sales, filterable by date range, product, buyer email, order id, customer name or license key. Each row is a full purchase record: price and fee in the smallest unit of the SALE'S OWN currency, buyer email, variants chosen, answers to custom fields, UTM parameters, subscription state, affiliate credit and any license key. The window is after and before as YYYY-MM-DD dates, and pagination is the opaque next_page_key cursor with no page size to tune. The currency is per row rather than per account, which matters before adding any of these numbers up. Requires view_sales. Gumroad: List Tax Forms gumroad_list_tax_forms List the tax forms Gumroad has generated for the seller, currently 1099-K and 1099-MISC, each with its year, type and filing timestamp. A null filed_at means the form exists but has not been filed yet. This is US ONLY and only for sellers with the tax centre enabled, so an account outside that will get nothing back rather than an explanation. Asking for a year outside the seller's available range, which runs from the account creation year to last year, returns 404. Requires the view_tax_data scope. Gumroad: List Upcoming Payouts gumroad_list_upcoming_payouts Fetch the payouts that have not been paid yet. There can be at most two at any moment. Every row has a NULL id and a payable status because these have not happened, so the amounts are forecasts that can still move as sales, refunds and chargebacks land: do not store them as though they were settled figures. Requires the view_payouts scope. Gumroad: List Variant Categories gumroad_list_variant_categories List a product's variant categories. A category is the GROUPING, for example Colors or Tier, and the individual options inside it are variants. For a tiered membership the category is usually the single Tier group and each membership tier is a variant. This is the source for every variant category picker in this connector. Requires view_profile, edit_products or account. Gumroad: List Variants gumroad_list_variants List the options inside one variant category, with each one's name, price difference in the smallest currency unit and purchase cap. This is the source for every variant picker in this connector, and it needs both the product and the category first because a variant only means something inside its own category. Requires view_profile, edit_products or account. Gumroad: List Workflows gumroad_list_workflows List the seller's ACTIVE workflows, newest first, with each one's audience type, trigger, product, state, step count and audience filters. Only active workflows are returned, so this is not a complete inventory of everything ever built. It is the source for the workflow picker on the two workflow email nodes. Requires edit_emails or account. Gumroad: Verify License gumroad_verify_license Check whether a license key is valid for a product, and get back the purchase behind it: buyer email, price, quantity, subscription state, refund and dispute flags, and the number of times the key has been used. This is the ONE endpoint on the whole Gumroad API that needs no credential and no OAuth application at all, which is why it can run from a customer's own machine. Watch increment_uses_count: it DEFAULTS TO TRUE, so every plain check burns a seat on a multi seat license. Set it off for a read only check such as a dashboard poll. Read the refunded, disputed and subscription_ended_at fields as well as the success flag, because a valid key can belong to a refunded purchase. Action nodes 48 Gumroad: Abort File Upload gumroad_abort_file_upload Cancel a multipart upload that failed partway through, so the half uploaded parts are not left behind. Read the status field in the response, because it has two meanings and only one of them is final: accepted means S3 took the cancellation but parts still in flight may land seconds later, and already_gone means there is no multipart session for this upload_id. Call this again while you see accepted, and stop when you see already gone. Requires edit_products. Gumroad: Add Product Cover gumroad_add_product_cover Add a cover to a product from a publicly reachable URL. Gumroad FETCHES the URL server side and stores its own copy, so the URL has to be reachable over HTTP or HTTPS from the public internet: a private link or a presigned upload URL will not work. Images in JPEG, PNG and GIF are accepted, and so are video URLs including YouTube and Vimeo, which come back as an oembed cover. This is a PUBLICLY VISIBLE change: the cover appears on the product page as soon as it is stored. The response returns the full cover list and the main_cover_id; reorder them with the cover_ids field on Gumroad: Update Product. Gumroad has no idempotency mechanism, so running this node twice creates two records. Guard retries on your side. Requires edit_products. Gumroad: Add Workflow Email gumroad_create_workflow_email Add one email step to an existing workflow, without changing whether the workflow is published. The new step inherits the workflow's state, and that is the part that reaches people: on a PUBLISHED workflow whose send_to_past_customers is true, adding a step SCHEDULES IT FOR ELIGIBLE PAST CUSTOMERS, so a step added to a year old onboarding sequence can go out to everyone who ever bought. Check the workflow's state and that flag first. Abandoned cart workflows do not accept added steps at all. Gumroad has no idempotency mechanism, so running this node twice creates two records. Guard retries on your side. Requires edit_emails or account. Gumroad: Complete File Upload gumroad_complete_file_upload Step 3 of 4: finalize the multipart upload started by Gumroad: Presign File Upload by submitting the ETag of every part. The S3 object is not usable until this succeeds. The returned file_url is the CANONICAL url and the only value that can be attached to a product, so store it: reading the product back later gives a time limited signed URL instead and the canonical one cannot be recovered from a read. Step 4 is passing that URL to Gumroad: Create Product or Gumroad: Update Product. Requires edit_products. Gumroad: Create Custom Field gumroad_create_custom_field Add an extra question to a product's checkout, for example a phone number or a Twitter handle. A PUBLICLY VISIBLE change: the field appears at checkout immediately, and marking it required means a buyer cannot complete a purchase without answering. Whatever buyers enter is returned on the sale record under custom_fields, so only ask for what you need. The name doubles as the identifier for later updates and deletes. Gumroad has no idempotency mechanism, so running this node twice creates two records. Guard retries on your side. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Create Email gumroad_create_email Create an audience email. By default it is a DRAFT and nothing is sent, which is the safe way to use this node. Setting publish to true, or draft to false, SENDS IT IMMEDIATELY to the chosen audience, which can be every follower and customer the seller has, and there is no recall. Scheduling is a separate step on an existing email rather than an option here. Gumroad has no idempotency mechanism, so running this node twice creates two records. Guard retries on your side. A retried run with publish on sends the campaign twice. Requires edit_emails or account. Gumroad: Create Offer Code gumroad_create_offer_code Create a discount code. name is the text a buyer types at checkout, so it becomes usable the moment this succeeds and anyone who learns it can redeem it: treat a generated code as live money off. amount_off is read together with offer_type, which defaults to cents, so 100 with the default means one dollar off in USD while 100 with percent means free. Set universal to apply it to EVERY product on the account rather than only this one. Cap the blast radius with max_purchase_count. Gumroad has no idempotency mechanism, so running this node twice creates two records. Guard retries on your side. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Create Product gumroad_create_product Create a product as a DRAFT. It is not visible to buyers until Gumroad: Enable Product publishes it, which makes this the safe half of a two-step publish. native_type is fixed at creation and can never be changed afterwards, so choose it deliberately. Prices are in the smallest unit of the currency, so 100 means one dollar in USD. Covers and thumbnails are attached separately, and files need the four-call upload flow first. Gumroad has no idempotency mechanism, so running this node twice creates two records. Guard retries on your side. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Create Resource Subscription gumroad_create_resource_subscription Subscribe a URL of yours to one kind of Gumroad event, so Gumroad POSTs to it whenever that event happens. This MANAGES GUMROAD'S OWN WEBHOOKS and is not a Mattering trigger: the endpoint you name has to exist and be reachable before this is useful. Eight resources are supported: sale, refund, dispute, dispute_won, cancellation, subscription_updated, subscription_ended and subscription_restarted. The sale, refund, dispute and dispute_won payloads follow Gumroad's Ping format; the four subscription payloads carry subscription_id, product_id, product_name, user_id, user_email and purchase_ids plus their own fields. Subscribing to sales requires the view_sales scope specifically. Gumroad has no idempotency mechanism, so running this node twice creates two records. Guard retries on your side. Gumroad: Create Variant gumroad_create_variant Add one option to a variant category, for example Red inside Colors, or Premium inside Tier. A PUBLICLY VISIBLE change: the option appears in the chooser on the product page immediately and can be bought. price_difference_cents is a DIFFERENCE from the base price, in the smallest currency unit, not an absolute price, so 250 adds 2.50 on top in a currency with minor units. Gumroad has no idempotency mechanism, so running this node twice creates two records. Guard retries on your side. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Create Variant Category gumroad_create_variant_category Create a variant category on a product, which is the group buyers choose from at checkout, for example Colors or Format. The category on its own does nothing until it has options: add those with Gumroad: Create Variant. A PUBLICLY VISIBLE change once options exist, because it adds a chooser to the product page. Gumroad has no idempotency mechanism, so running this node twice creates two records. Guard retries on your side. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Decrement License Uses Count gumroad_decrement_license_uses_count Give a seat back on a multi seat license by lowering its uses count by one. This is the deactivate half of a seat management flow: when a customer uninstalls on one machine, call this so they can activate on another without buying more seats. It pairs with the increment that Gumroad: Verify License performs by default. Gumroad: Delete Custom Field gumroad_delete_custom_field PERMANENTLY delete a checkout question. It disappears from the product's checkout immediately and Gumroad documents no undelete. Answers already captured on past sales are part of those sale records rather than of this field, so removing the question stops collecting new answers rather than erasing old ones. The field is addressed by its name in the URL and a name with spaces is percent encoded for you. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Delete Email gumroad_delete_email PERMANENTLY delete an audience email, draft or published. Gumroad documents no undelete, so the copy is gone. Deleting a published email does not unsend it: the messages already delivered stay in recipients' inboxes, and a published email can also have a public page on the seller's profile, which this removes. Requires edit_emails or account. Gumroad: Delete Media File gumroad_delete_media Delete a file from the media library. The file leaves the library immediately and the hosted copy is queued for removal, so ANY PAGE STILL EMBEDDING ITS URL will show a broken image once the purge runs. Because media files are account wide rather than per product, that can be several product pages and the profile at once, and nothing in the API tells you which. Not reversible: restoring means uploading the original again, which produces a new id and a new URL. Requires edit_profile specifically. Gumroad: Delete Offer Code gumroad_delete_offer_code PERMANENTLY delete a discount code. The code stops working at checkout immediately, so anyone who has been given it and has not yet redeemed it will be turned away: check times_used against what you expected before running this in a campaign teardown. Gumroad documents no undelete. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Delete Product gumroad_delete_product PERMANENTLY delete a product. Gumroad documents no undelete and this API has no restore endpoint, so this is not recoverable from a workflow. Existing buyers, their sales records and their library access are outside what this call promises to preserve, so treat it as an operator action rather than an automated one. If the goal is only to stop selling, use Gumroad: Disable Product, which takes the product off sale and is reversible. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Delete Product Cover gumroad_delete_product_cover Remove a cover from a product. A PUBLICLY VISIBLE change that takes effect on the product page immediately, and it is not reversible from this API: Gumroad stores its own copy of the image and deleting the cover discards it, so restoring means adding the original source URL again. The response returns the remaining covers and the new main_cover_id, which is null once the last cover is gone. Requires edit_products. Gumroad: Delete Product Thumbnail gumroad_delete_product_thumbnail Remove a product's thumbnail so it falls back to Gumroad's default. A PUBLICLY VISIBLE change, live immediately, and not reversible from this API: the stored image is discarded, so restoring means setting it again from the original source. Requires edit_products. Gumroad: Delete Resource Subscription gumroad_delete_resource_subscription Unsubscribe from a Gumroad event, so it stops POSTing to your endpoint. The events themselves keep happening, they just stop being delivered, and Gumroad does not replay what was missed while a subscription was gone: anything that occurs between this call and a re-subscribe is simply not delivered. Re-subscribing creates a new subscription with a new id. Gumroad: Delete Variant gumroad_delete_variant PERMANENTLY delete one option from a variant category. A PUBLICLY VISIBLE change: the option disappears from the product page and can no longer be bought. Gumroad documents no undelete, and on a tiered membership the variant IS a tier, so removing one affects the members on it. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Delete Variant Category gumroad_delete_variant_category PERMANENTLY delete a variant category. This removes the whole chooser from the product page, and the variants inside it go with it, so this is much larger than deleting one option. Gumroad documents no undelete. On a tiered membership the category IS the tier structure, so removing it changes what existing members are on: do not run this against a live membership from an automation. Requires edit_products or account. Gumroad: Disable License gumroad_disable_license Disable a license key.
